explanation: The OK sign (thumb and index finger forming a circle) is understood as a positive, everyday gesture for 'fine' or 'good' in the Netherlands, as in most of Western Europe. It carries none of the vulgar or offensive meanings it has in some other countries.
local_tip: Use it freely to mean 'all good' or 'okay' in casual conversation.

also_check.note: The gesture is considered a vulgar insult, similar in severity to showing the middle finger.
In parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East, including Turkey, the gesture can be read as a vulgar or homophobic insult.
The gesture commonly means 'money' as well as 'OK', and is generally understood positively.
